purpose: RFC-2026-029 (approved 2026-10-11) decides the application tier's stack, allowlist, lockfile policy and layout, and names WP-1A-A0-002 as the package that installs the first dependency and makes its §8 acceptance conditions real. This package installs the minimum set (next, react, react-dom; typescript, @types/node, @types/react, @types/react-dom, tailwindcss, @tailwindcss/postcss, postcss, vitest) at exact versions under npm 11.19.0 and Node 24.20.0 with --ignore-scripts, --engine-strict and a seven-day --before; creates apps/web as an npm workspace with one App Router page and no data path; adds tsconfig with the §2.1 flags and `npm run typecheck`; adds dependency-free guards for §8/1, §8/2, the licences, §8/4 and §8/5 with tests and negative controls; and adds the CI steps RFC-2026-029 §4.6, §4.8 and §8 and RFC-2026-034 §8 item 4 name.

include: The first install: package.json (workspaces, devDependencies, typecheck and test:app scripts), apps/web/package.json and the root package-lock.json

apps/web: App Router layout and page, the page's test, Tailwind CSS through postcss.config.mjs and a CSS @import, next.config.ts with telemetry off and unoptimized images, apps/web/types/next.d.ts and a .gitignore for next-env.d.ts
tsconfig.base.json with RFC-2026-029 §2.1/2's flags, tsconfig.json for `npm run typecheck`, apps/web/tsconfig.json for next build, vitest.config.ts

Guards: scripts/verify-app-dependencies.mjs (§8/1, §8/2, licences, §4.8's day count), scripts/verify-app-boundaries.mjs with its rules in scripts/app-boundaries.mjs and its parsed reader in scripts/app-boundaries-parser.mjs (§8/4, §2.1/3, §8/5, path aliases refused, build configuration held to allowlisted shapes), scripts/verify-app-build-graph.mjs (§6.3 on what next build included), scripts/verify-typecheck-control.mjs (§8/3), scripts/verify-release-age.mjs (§4.8), their data scripts/app-dependency-allowlist.json, their suites and the typecheck control's fixture

CI: in the bootstrap job, the test-integrity guard and then npm run check with no node_modules (§8/6), before the clean install; in a separate application job that needs the bootstrap job, its own clean install, the two guards (the boundary guard with --require-parser), the type check and its control, the application tests, the boundary guard again immediately before the build (A1-257-10), the web build and then the build-graph check of what it included, npm audit and the release age
RFC-2026-029 Amendment 2026-10-12 recording the Owner's licence decision and his widening of §3.2's typescript cell to scripts/app-boundaries-parser.mjs, and its disposition record
The §8/8 record of each installed name's licence, install script, packages added, network use and telemetry

acceptance_criteria: §8/1: every package.json's direct dependencies are compared with scripts/app-dependency-allowlist.json, a machine-readable copy of RFC-2026-029 §3.1/§3.2 including the 'where it may be imported' column, and a test fails when that copy and the RFC's tables disagree.

§8/2: every version in every package.json is exact, and every resolved lockfile entry is from https://registry.npmjs.org/ with a sha512 integrity; an inBundle entry is accepted only inside a registry parent that lists it in bundleDependencies.
§8/3: `npm run typecheck` is `tsc --noEmit` over tsconfig.base.json's §2.1/2 flags, runs in CI, and its negative control fails on a fixture with one marked error per flag.

§8/4: the §6.3 boundaries are checked by a guard script (ESLint deferred by the Owner), each with a negative control: dependency-free in npm run check, and read by TypeScript's parser in CI with its own negative controls held first. While ESLint is deferred the same guard holds §2.1/3 (no @ts-ignore or @ts-nocheck, @ts-expect-error only with a reason, no `any` in application code) and refuses path aliases (Q-029-1), holds every build configuration to an allowlisted shape, and after next build checks what the build included against §6.3 (A1-257-7).

§8/5: no supabase/migrations directory; no file under apps/ or src/ names the service role or its key; no file under apps/web names the worker credential, and none outside apps/worker/composition/** reads it; each with a negative control.

§8/6: npm run check passes with no node_modules, shown by a CI step before the clean install and after the workflow's own test-integrity guard step; no tooling module imports a package except the boundary guard's parsed reader, which only the CLI loads and no test reaches.
§8/8: per installed allowlisted name, from the resolved lockfile: licence, install script, packages added, network use at build or run time, telemetry and its switch.
§8/9 and §4.8: CI checks the publish age of every lockfile entry a pull request adds or changes; §4.6: CI runs npm audit --include=dev --audit-level=high.
Every lockfile licence is in §3.4/2's list or covered by Amendment 2026-10-12's named transitive exceptions, held by a guard with a negative control.

RFC-2026-034 §8 item 4: CI runs the application tests (vitest run, passWithNoTests false) on every head, in the application job, which runs every step that executes an installed package after the bootstrap job's guards and on a runner of its own.
npm run check stays green, and the toolchain stays Node 24.20.0 / npm 11.19.0.

RFC-2026-029 §8/4 asks for the §6.3 boundaries as lint errors. The Product Owner deferred ESLint on 2026-10-12 with the option `ไม่ใส่ตอนนี้ (Recommended)` ("check the import boundaries (§6.3) with a guard script that has no dependency instead"), and RFC-2026-029's Amendment 2026-10-12 records that answer, in the option's words, as how §8/4 is held while ESLint is deferred; the disposition §3 (b) says the same. A0's reading, marked as such in both: the same guard also holds §2.1/3 (no @ts-ignore, a reasoned @ts-expect-error, no `any`) and stands as §2.1/4's lint step while ESLint is deferred, and in CI it reads the sources with TypeScript's parser through the installed `typescript` package. That import is no longer A0's reading: the Owner allowed it on 2026-10-12 (answered 07:24:27Z), and Amendment 2026-10-12 widens §3.2's typescript cell to scripts/app-boundaries-parser.mjs only (C0-257-1, C0-257-2, R0-257-2).

RFC-2026-029 §10 questions handed to this package: Q-029-1 is not measured here, because no src/ exists; it is owed to the first package that creates src/, which also adds src/** to tsconfig.json's include and teaches the boundary guard the alias it chooses (until then every path alias is refused). Q-029-5: next-intl is not installed; it is the shell's (WP-1A-A5-003). Q-029-7: none of its packages was needed (no ESLint, so no typescript-eslint; the page test renders with react-dom/server; no server-only or tw-animate-css), and the parsed boundary guard stands where lint would have stood; no allowlist amendment for it travels here.

Known limitation (R0-257-3): npm run check fails (exit 70) on a working tree where `next build` has run, because scripts/scan-repository-secrets.mjs walks apps/web/.next/. CI is not affected (the build runs in the application job, after and apart from npm run check); locally, delete apps/web/.next first. Whether the scanner skips .next is owed by its owner, WP-0A-A0-003; this package does not edit the scanner.

The worker credential's environment variable is named nowhere yet. scripts/app-dependency-allowlist.json reserves WORKER_DATABASE_URL (with RFC-2026-028's app_worker_login) so that the §8/5 guard holds something; WP-1A-A0-004 uses that name or changes it there in the same pull request.
